'When this defends and the attacking hero has played or activated a reaction this chain link, create a Bloodrot Pox token under their control.'

DELIVERY: ON_DEFEND is dispatched to the defending card object itself (engine._dsl_defend_listener -> dispatch(card_obj.slug)), so the trap hears its own defend.

CONDITION: REACTION_THIS_LINK player=ATTACKING, no kind filter = 'has played or activated A reaction' (any kind) by combat.attacker_id this chain link. Ability-level conditions evaluate at RESOLUTION (interpreter._run_ability), which matches the release note that the reaction check happens when the trap resolves and becomes a defending card - not at trigger time. The data source is live: play._record_reaction_on_link appends to combat.reactions_this_link for both played and activated reactions, and the list is link-scoped by construction (new CombatState per attack).

EFFECT: CREATE_TOKEN reads token/amount/player (handler verified); player=OPPONENT resolves to 3 - controller, i.e. the attacking hero - 'under their control'. Token definition already exists at json/tokens/bloodrot_pox.json (END_OF_TURN destroy-or-pay static), so no destination param is needed; zone routing derives from the template subtypes.

INEXPRESSIBLE CLAUSE: the release note 'If there is no attacking hero (e.g. this is defending against an ally attack), this does not trigger.' No condition asks whether the ATTACKER is a hero - ATTACK_TARGET_IS_HERO asks about the attack's TARGET. Ally attacks exist in this engine and their combat.attacker_id is the controlling PLAYER, so on an ally attack this gate would read the ally-controller's reactions and can fire where the printed card would not. Would need an ATTACKER_IS_HERO-style condition to close.
